div.head: Rect 9, 9.1
div.ab: [9] Be wifmonna metsunge. Ðeowan wifmen: VIII pund cornes to mete, I sceap oððe III p.' to wintersufle, I syster beana to længtensufle, hwæig on sumera oððe I p.' [9.1] Eallum æhtemannum gebyreð Midwintres feorm ⁊ Eastorfeorm, sulhæcer ⁊ hærfesthand[f]ul toeacan heora nydrihte.

Uni ancille: VIII pondia annone ad uictum, I ouem uel III d. ad hiemale companagium, I sester fabe ad quadragesimalem conuictum, in estate suum hƿeig uel I d. [9.1] Omnibus ehtemannis iure competit Natalis firma et paschalis, sulhæcer (id est carruce acra) et manipulus Augusti in augmentum iure debiti recti.

be wifmonna | metsunge Đeowan wifmen .viii. pund cornes to mete .i. sceap oððe .iii. peningas to wintersufle .i. syster beana to længtensufle .hwæig on sumera . oððe .i. peninga. eallum æhtemannum gebyreð mid|wintres feorm. 7 eastorfeorm. sulhæcer . 7 hærfesthandsul . to eacan heora nydrihte .

Be wifmonna metsunge Ðeowan wifmen: VIII pund cornes to mete, I sceap oððe III pæniga to wintersufle, I syster beana to længtensufle, hwæig on sumera oððe I pænig. [9.1] Eallum æhtemannum gebyreð Midwintres feorm and Eastorfeorm, sulhæcer and hærfesthandful toeacan heora nydrihte.

Von Beköstigung [höriger] Weiber. Der unfreien Frau: 8 ‘Pfund’ [genannte Getreidelasten] Korn [jährlich] als Nahrung, 1 Schaf oder 3 Pfennig als Winter-Zukost, 1 Sextar Bohnen als Zukost für Fasten, Molken im Sommer oder 1 Pfennig. [9.1] Allen leibeigenen Leuten gebührt ein Weihnachtsschmaus und ein Osterschmaus, ein bepflügbarer Acker [Landes] und [täglich?] in der Ernte eine Handvoll [Korn] neben ihrer nothwendigen [Mindest]gebühr.

[9] Of the food allowance of [unfree] women. To the unfree woman: 8 ‘pounds’ [i.e. loads] of grain [yearly] as food, 1 sheep or 3 pence as winter relish, 1 sester of beans as relish for Lent, whey in summer or 1 penny. [9.1] To all slaves is due a Christmas feast and an Easter feast, a plough-acre [of land] and [daily?] a handful [of grain] at harvest, besides their necessary [minimum] due.

Concerning the provisioning of women Bound women [are due] eight pounds of corn as food, one sheep or three pennies as provisions for midwinter, one sester of beans as spring provisions, whey in the summer or one penny. To all bound men are due winter provisions, and Easter provisions, a strip of land for ploughing, and a harvest handful, [and] to each their necessities.

Regarding the Feeding of the Women Female servants are due eight pounds of grain as food, one sheep or three pennies as supplies for winter, one sester of beans as supplies for spring, and whey in the summer or one penny. [9.1] All enslaved people are due meals for Christmas and Easter, an allotment of land for farming, a portion of the harvest, as well as their necessities.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 9–9.1. K: ‘XIII pund’ corrected to ‘VIII pund’ against Liebermann. B reads ‘mets’ in the heading and ‘hærfesthand[f]ul’ as ‘-ndsul’. Liebermann compares the Borley custom: ‘de auena quantum potest in manu palmare’; and Rect 8, 4.1 and 21.4.
